motions.item_title: Appoint Jacob Adams to the Youth Council fulfilling a term through June 30, 2025
motions.motion: Councilmember Grey moved to appoint Jacob Adams to the Youth Council fulfilling a term through June 30, 2025. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Jacob Adams appointed to Youth Council
motions.summary: The council appointed Jacob Adams to the Youth Council for a term running through June 30, 2025.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this fills a seat on the city's youth advisory body.

motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve the consent agenda, removing Items 11.C. and 11.E. from the consent agenda and placing them at the end of the scheduled items for further discussion. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Two items pulled for separate discussion
motions.summary: The council approved its consent agenda but pulled the civic campus land purchase and the lobbying contract out for individual discussion.
motions.impact: This is procedural housekeeping — it only means two items got their own debate instead of passing in a batch.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Title 17 Energy-Related Code Amendments
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to table an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Title 17 Energy-Related Code Amendments. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Energy code changes put on hold
motions.summary: The council delayed a decision on changes to the city's energy-related building and land use rules in Title 17.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for now — the existing rules stay in place until the council brings the item back.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Purchase Agreement with Ivory Homes and SITLA to purchase 20.99 acres of Land for a Future Civic Campus
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Purchase Agreement with Ivory Homes and SITLA to purchase 20.99 acres of Land for a Future Civic Campus with the following changes: 1. Amending references to Fionnuala Kofoed, City Recorder to the new City Recorder, Gina Olsen 2. Strike any restriction/language on commercial size restrictions. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion. Discussion took place regarding the size restrictions, drive-throughs/deed restrictions, and what would be considered a “Public Works” facility.
motions.headline: Buy 21 acres for a future civic campus
motions.summary: The council took up an agreement with Ivory Homes and SITLA to buy 20.99 acres for a future civic campus, with limits on commercial building size struck from the deal.
motions.impact: If the purchase goes through, the city would own land it intends to use for future public buildings. Nothing changes for you now — no buildings, timeline, or price are set in this item.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving an Agreement to Provide Lobbying Services
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving an Agreement to Provide Lobbying Services for one year at a rate of $60,000 annually. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: City hires a lobbyist for $60,000 a year
motions.summary: The city signed a one-year, $60,000 contract for lobbying services to represent Eagle Mountain's interests.
motions.impact: Nothing changes day to day — this is the city paying an outside firm to advocate for it, most likely at the state level.
